_comment: Copy to <your-project>/pipeline.json and edit. 'base' must be your project root (absolute). Every other path is relative to 'base' unless absolute. Decision files are the single source of truth; this config only tells the scripts where things live and how files are named.
_batch_comment: Batch/date of finished goods. Set per run via env BATCH_DATE or edit here. Ledgers are NOT dated - they always live in xlsx_dir.
_lang_comment: code = decision-file code; name = the Chinese/canonical label shown in the ledger and used in product filenames; font = actual output font for that language. IMPORTANT: languages with regional variants must be confirmed with the user BEFORE building (see SKILL.md step 0) and listed as separate entries: Portuguese = ptbr (Brazil, onibus) vs ptpt (Europe, autocarro); Spanish = eses (Spain) vs esmx/esar (Latin America); English = enus/enuk; Chinese = zhcn/zhtw. Never collapse variants into one 'Portuguese'/'Spanish' entry - the translations differ word by word. Optional per-language 'font_file' gives the exact TTF/OTF path used to measure glyph widths (absolute, or relative to 'base'; e.g. C:/Windows/Fonts/ARLRDBD.TTF). If omitted, the font is resolved by its INTERNAL name (family/full/PostScript) inside 'font_dir' - Windows file names like ARLRDBD.TTF do not contain the readable name, so this lookup reads the name table. If nothing matches, the scripts stop with a message telling you to set font_file. IMPORTANT: measuring MUST use the font that will actually be typeset in Illustrator, otherwise width/wrap decisions are wrong.
_color_comment: no = the serial number embedded in source/product filenames; pages = expected PDF page count for verification; name = label used in filenames.

files.source_ai: D7_点读启蒙卡片_{no}{color_name}背景（美式英语）.ai

_schema_comment: Key names inside each decision JSON. Leave as-is unless your decision generator uses different keys.
_gate_comment: Decision completeness gate. cx (target horizontal centre measured from the source artwork) is ALWAYS required: without it the JSX skips centring and outputs misaligned words. sz is not required AND is rejected for body labels: only a card title may change size (titles are fitted to their oval by the JSX, never taken from `sz`). Set allow_body_sz=true only for artwork where uneven body sizes are acceptable -- it also unlocks tuning.sizefix. require_sz=true forces every entry to carry sz (i.e. it requires allow_body_sz as well).
_jsx_comment: JSX generator settings. generator is a command template receiving lang/color; runner is the PowerShell batch script.
_geometry_export_comment: Size gates for classifying page objects when exporting geometry from a NEW layout. export_geometry.py injects these into geometry_export_template.jsx. Run 'python export_geometry.py <color> --no-run' then inspect geom_<color>.tsv counts (labels/illus/titles per artboard) and tune until they match the real artwork. illus_above=false for layouts where the illustration sits BELOW its label. This is the ONLY step that is layout-specific.
_decision_engine_comment: Layout-agnostic placement thresholds used by build_decisions.py. Defaults are the proven values; tune only if the new artwork uses very different spacing. All in points. base_size is the source font size the translations table was measured against.
_decision_tuning_comment: OPTIONAL project-specific fixes, file named by files.decision_tuning. A new project may leave it empty - the engine still produces full cx/dy/sz. 'pos' holds reviewer hand-edit shifts applied to cx/dy at write time, so a clean rebuild reproduces hand placement; key is '<ab>|<en>'. NOTE: sizefix is IGNORED unless gate.allow_body_sz=true (body type is fixed). Format: {short:{lang:{en:val}}, sizefix:{lang:{en:pt}}, compound:{...}, titles:{lang:{en:val}}, pos:{lang:{color:{'<ab>|<en>':{dx,dy}}}}}.
_vector_text_comment: Labels drawn as OUTLINED vector paths have no text layer, so export_spans cannot find them and they would ship untranslated. Declare each here: color, page (1-based), en (translation-table key), box=[x0,y0,x1,y1] in ILLUSTRATOR EXPANDED coords (diagnose by listing groupItems matching the label area), size. make_jsx deletes the matching group(s) and typesets the translation in place. Leave [] if the artwork has no outlined text.
_vector_text_engine_comment: Tuning for locating an outlined label's group and choosing a body-label frame as the replacement template. Defaults suit an 18pt-label deck; change to match your artwork's body size. center_tol_pt/size_tol_pt: bbox match tolerances. template_size_min_pt/max_pt: acceptable body font size when picking a template frame.
_geometry_comment: Layout constraints injected into the JSX. Values below are proven on the D7 book; tune per source artwork. title_fit: shrink+centre titles inside the real ellipse (found by scanning pathItems). Word overflow is REPORTED only (BODY-OVERFLOW in the log) -- body type is never resized. ink_bounds_words makes the JSX re-measure ink instead of visibleBounds (slower but more accurate). Obstacles: decision JSON may carry 'obstacles' per artboard as [[x0,y0,x1,y1],...]; ocap=0 only WARNS in the log, >0 moves the label down (away from the art above it) by at most that many points. Keep ocap=0 if your decision engine already resolved collisions. title_wrap_size: font size used when a title must take two lines (default = the source's own two-line title size).

geometry._title_two_comment: TWO-LINE titles only. title_two_fill = the share of the oval's radius a multi-line block may use, where (x/a)^2+(y/b)^2 = 1 means touching the boundary. 1.0 (default) never shrinks a title that already fits -- the block is centred on the oval and the lines are judged one by one, so a widest line may reach the curve at its own height and no further. Lower it only if you deliberately want a margin and accept the title getting smaller (0.9 costs ~5% of the size). title_two_balance = how much of the clearance-equalising downward shift to apply (0 = keep the block geometrically centred, which is the look that holds; 1 = equalise the corner clearance of the two lines, which fixes crowding but drops the block visibly low).

_layout_comment: Body type is FIXED: no key here can shrink a body word. A label that does not fit is wrapped, shifted, short-formed (translations '<lang>_short') or reported for rewording. min_scale is only the severity threshold of the FIT report (a word needing to be under 72% of its size to fit is treated as 'cannot fit'), NOT a shrink factor. The title_pill_*/title_top_pt/title_pout/title_center_tol_pt/title_glyph keys describe how the POST-BUILD gate (qa_output.py) finds a pill title in the finished vector artwork: set them per artwork, otherwise the gate finds nothing and reports TITLE-UNREAD instead of passing silently.
